thread:
Arjun: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC meeting earlier — we need to decide how aggressive we get with Triton-first vs continuing with CUDA/CUTLASS maintenance. TL;DR: Triton gives fast iteration and custom fusions, but Cutlass/CUDA still wins in some tiled GEMM patterns and has more stable perf on Ampere/Blackwell for larger heads.

Sam: Agreed. My main concern is long-term maintenance cost. Triton prototypes are great but we keep hitting edge-case divergences across NCCL+multi-GPU and some of our fallback paths.

Lia: From infra perspective: Triton binaries mean we push a lot more custom kernels to packages which complicates packaging and reproducible images. Cutlass builds are heavier but more static.

Maria: For real workloads we care about: 1) causal self-attention latency at short sequences, 2) KV-cache memory churn for streaming, 3) mixed-precision stability (fp8/fp16), and 4) cross-GPU pipelining. Any benchmark plan should target those explicitly.

Arjun: Proposed concrete plan (short):
- Build a compact microbench harness that runs: fused causal-attn (different head sizes), unfused attention (GEMM+softmax), and Cutlass fused kernels.
- Add KV-cache stress tests that simulate many small seq appends and evictions.
- Run mixed-precision fuzzing with tiny gradients to catch numerical regressions.
- Collect Nsight timelines + per-token occupancy.

Sam: +1. Action items: I can wire up the harness in runtime/tests/kernel_bench. Need naming conventions and metrics. Suggest metrics: p50/p95/allocs-per-token/peak-alloc.

Lia: I'll scope packaging implications. If we pick Triton-heavy path, we should add a build matrix entry and a pinned triton wheel version in images. Also we need a rollback plan to use CUDA kernels if a binary mismatch occurs.

Maria: We should also define an API boundary: runtime should call a single AttentionBackend interface that exposes: init(cfg), run(attn_args), kv_swap(...), and profile_hint(buf). That makes runtime switch trivial.

Arjun: Good point — interface boundaries were a key RFC item. Let's standardize error codes for fallback so we can trigger runtime-level fallbacks without panics. Example: E_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE, E_OOM_SOFT, E_NUMERIC_LIKELY.

InfraBot: perf-test started: run_id=rt-kbench-20260320-11, kernels=[triton,cutlass,cuda], devices=[a100-40gb-x4].

Sam: For the harness, can we include a synthetic request generator that replays real traces? I have a clean trace from our streaming demo.

Arjun: Yes — include trace replayer. Default configs: batch sizes [1,4,8,16], seq_len [8,32,128,512], head_size [64,128], num_heads [12,16,32].

Lia: Question: do we want to invest in hand-optimized CUTLASS kernels for the fused path or rely on CUTLASS primitives + small glue code? CUTLASS hand-tuning could be high ROI on Blackwell.

Maria: Let's measure before committing. Action: add a CUTLASS-primitive baseline and a hand-tuned candidate. If hand-tuned is >15% better on 2/3 hardware targets we'll consider landing it.

Sam: I'll take the harness + CI integration (action: sam -> PR in runtime/tests by EOD Friday).

Arjun: I'll draft the AttentionBackend interface RFC update and error-code enum.

Lia: I'll add packaging checklist and image matrix changes to eng-infra backlog (link: https://go/redwood/infra-builds).

Maria: I'll own the KV-cache stress test and the mixed-precision fuzz harness.

InfraBot: perf-test completed: run_id=rt-kbench-20260320-11, status=partial, notes="triton wins small-seq p50, cutlass better at seq>=128; occasional triton small-ooms seen".

Arjun: Nice, please post raw logs. Next sync: quick 30m on Thursday to review numbers and decide whether to prototype a CUTLASS hand-tuned path.

Sam: Posted initial graphs: https://perf.redwood/internal/rt-kbench-20260320-11. Looks like for head_size=64 triton is ~12% faster at seq<=32 but Cutlass overtakes by 18% at 128.

Lia: Noted. I'll prep migration checklist for images if we go Triton-first.

Maria: I'll add test failure thresholds: if numeric error > 1e-3 in relative L2 or perplexity regression > 2% we block rollout.

Arjun: Thanks all. Summary of action items: Sam -> harness + CI PR, Arjun -> interface RFC update, Maria -> KV + mixed-precision tests, Lia -> packaging/image matrix + rollback plan. We'll reconvene after perf graphs. :thumbsup:
